messages:
maria: Quick heads-up — realtime-v2 circuit breaker is at canary (5%). If we need to drop to 0% immediately, who is authorized to do the flip and what minimal audit evidence do we need? :warning:

alex_r: Authorization: eng-oncall leads + eng-platform SREs only. Pls don't ask individual ICs to flip unless an oncall lead delegates. Procedure: post a short rationale in #incidents, ping @eng-platform, then flip. The flip action must include: reason, deploy id, and rollback window.

sam: Add the exact CLI we use so folks don't improvise. Example command we expect:```
flagctl flip realtime-v2 --percent 0 --reason "high-5xx-rate" --owner sam
```That populates the audit fields automatically.

ops-bot: Audit event queued -> event_id=ev_20260317_7890, source=flagctl, actor=sam (pending commit). Logs will stream to kinesis://prod-audit/circuit-breaker and create jira INFR-4321 if percent==0.

jen: Escalation path if oncall lead unreachable: 1) contact eng-platform on-call by phone (doc in runbook), 2) if no answer in 10m escalate to SRE manager (@michael). Always capture attempted contact timestamps in the incident thread.

alex_r: Guardrails recap: automated rollback policy will re-open 5% after 30m unless manual ack. If you flip to 0% you must attach the monitoring snapshot (error-rate, p99 latency) and mark the incident as "circuit-breaker" type in the ticket.

sam: If someone does a flip, please also paste the exact command output into #incidents so we have the stdout/stderr. Example output format we look for:
```
> flagctl: realtime-v2 -> percent=0
> audit_id=ev_20260317_7890
> persisted to kinesis://prod-audit/circuit-breaker
```

maria: Good. I'll add a short checklist to the runbook (who-authorizes, CLI, audit path, escalation timeline). No flip now — keeping canary until we confirm the metric trend. Thanks everyone :white_check_mark:
